rationale: PINS the three proto2 constructs this analyzer had NO fixture for, and each of them is a place where a plausible analyzer fabricates something. (1) `extend Foo { … }` adds members to a type this file does not declare, so the block is NOT a declaration: minting a symbol for it produces a phantom type that then becomes the source of a fabricated containment edge and a second, disagreeing copy of a type that already has an owner in the file that declares it. The file carries both shapes — an extend of a type declared in the SAME file, and the corpus's real shape, an extend of the well-known `google.protobuf.MessageOptions` from an imported file. (2) A proto2 `group` declares a nested type AND a field of the same name in one declaration, so on a bare `owner.name` id the two collide and the `uses` edge that should run field-to-type loops a symbol onto itself. (3) `reserved` and `extensions` are facts about the SCHEMA rather than about a declaration — a retired field number is what makes a migration audit possible — so they attach to the owning message's metadata rather than becoming symbols or edges. PASS 2: two rows now require `meta.viaExtension` on the EDGE. It was on the symbol only, so the analyzer's own header claim that the edge carries it was false and a consumer reading the edge could not tell an extension field from a declared one.

the group's FIELD references the group's TYPE. Reading this edge the other way round, or collapsing both onto one id, is the self-loop the `#` disambiguator exists to prevent.

forbidRelationships.note: DELIBERATELY absent: the group's self-edge. It is the exact shape produced when the type and the field share one id, and a self-edge here is a symbol pointing at itself — which reads as a recursive type and poisons every graph consumer downstream.
protobuf has NO inheritance. `extend Foo` adds fields to Foo; it does not make anything a subclass, so an `extends` edge here would invent a language feature that does not exist.
same reason: there is no interface to satisfy in proto2.
